race_context: The 'Grant Marion Community School Board' races on the state list are for Marion Community Schools in Marion, Grant County. Federal data reported through PlainSchools show 3,668 students in 2024-25 and seven schools {plainschools_mcs}. The district also runs the Little Giants Preschool, the Grant Regional Career Center and the Walton Performing Arts Center {mcs_minutes_index}{mcs_min_20260714}.

The superintendent is Dr. Stephanie Lockwood {mcs_min_20260728}. The board approved her contract in December 2024, and the Chronicle-Tribune reported that she would start Jan. 4, 2025, replacing retiring superintendent Keith Burke {ct_dec2024}. On July 28, 2026, the board voted unanimously to extend her contract from June 30, 2028 to June 30, 2030 {mcs_min_20260728}.

The board has seven members who serve four-year terms, with elections every two years {mcs_about}. The district lists the members as Alan Beck (president, District I), Chuck Griffin (first vice president, District IV at-large), Shanna Bento (second vice president, District II), Gabe Delgado (secretary, District IV at-large), Dana Gault (District I), Richard Hart (District I) and Serafina Salamo (District III) {mcs_board}.

District 1 race: three seats, not one. The state list says 'vote for 1' {in_list}, but the Chronicle-Tribune's ballot list says 'District 1 (vote for 3)' {ct_ballot_2026}. The district lists three District I members whose terms end Dec. 31, 2026: Beck, Gault and Hart {mcs_board}. Beck and Hart are running again; Gault is not on the ballot {in_list}{ct_ballot_2026}. Four candidates are running for the three seats {in_list}{ct_ballot_2026}. In 2022 the Chronicle-Tribune also described District 1 as a three-seat race {ct_2022_qa}.

At-large race: one seat. The state list and the Chronicle-Tribune call it 'At Large, District 2' {in_list}{ct_ballot_2026}. The district's roster labels its at-large seats 'District IV (at-large)', and the at-large seat with a term ending Dec. 31, 2026 belongs to Chuck Griffin {mcs_board}. Griffin was appointed to the at-large seat in 2022 and was a candidate for it that November {ct_vacancies_2022}{ct_2022_qa}. He is not on the 2026 ballot, so the seat is open {in_list}{ct_ballot_2026}.

Budget and the 2025 property-tax law (July 2026): on July 14, 2026, the board unanimously approved moving $97,460.15 from the Debt Service Fund to the Operations Fund to account for the supplemental homestead credit {mcs_min_20260714}. Superintendent Lockwood told the board that the credit is money 'we will lose beginning in 2027' and described it as about a $300 loss per household {mcs_min_20260714}.

2027 budget (August-October 2026): on Aug. 11, 2026, the board moved its budget dates after the former chief financial officer left, and it approved a contract with Comprehensive Systems of Support for Schools to handle chief financial officer duties {mcs_min_20260811}. The new calendar set a public hearing for Sept. 22 and adoption for Oct. 27, 2026 {mcs_min_20260811}. At the Aug. 25 meeting, President Beck said the district was 'having to cut 3.7 million dollars' {mcs_min_20260825}. Marion Community Schools is not on the state's list of districts with a referendum in November 2026 {dlgf_ref_2026}. Two other Grant County districts, Mississinewa and Oak Hill, have operating referendums on the ballot {ct_ballot_2026}.

Facilities (August 2026): on Aug. 11, 2026, the board unanimously approved lease amendments through its building corporation to fund improvements in 2026-27 and 2027-28 {mcs_min_20260811}. Bond counsel said the improvements would focus on heating and air conditioning, lighting, flooring and wall coverings, with combined annual lease payments of no more than $3.6 million {mcs_min_20260811}. On Aug. 25 the board heard updates on storm damage to the Bill Green Athletic Arena, a replacement stadium scoreboard, the tennis courts, the track and lighting at the Walton Performing Arts Center {mcs_min_20260825}.

Curriculum and policy (2026): in September 2026 the board approved new curriculum, including Amplify CKLA for K-6 English language arts {mcs_min_20260908}. Revisions to the computer acceptable-use policy were discussed on Sept. 8 and held for a later meeting {mcs_min_20260908}. Collective-bargaining hearings with the Marion Teachers Association began on the same date {mcs_min_20260908}.
Forums: this guide found no 2026 candidate forum or questionnaire for these races. The Chronicle-Tribune printed a candidate list on Oct. 3, 2026 {ct_ballot_2026}.

candidates.summary: Incumbent and board president, seeking another term in District 1, where voters choose three members {mcs_board}{ct_ballot_2026}.
background: The district lists his occupation as 'Landscape designer, business owner of Comfort Landscapes' and says he joined the board in 2019 {mcs_board}.
In a 2022 Chronicle-Tribune questionnaire he described himself as a local business owner and lifelong Marion resident, and he said he had coached for 19 years {ct_2022_qa}.
path_to_ballot: Was elected in District 1 in 2018 and 2022, according to BallotReady {br_beck}.
Filed for reelection; The Indiana Citizen's copy of the state list gives June 4, 2026 as his filing date {incitizen_list}. The state lists him as Nonpartisan {in_list}.

items: At the July 14, 2026 meeting, discussing the homestead-credit transfer, he said: 'This SB1 is killing us in so many ways.' {mcs_min_20260714}

At the same meeting, Dr. Richard Hart asked whether the district could earn money from its facilities. Beck said the district should not have to 'come up with creative ways of making revenue to fund our operations' and called it 'a pipe dream' that facility rentals could pay for teacher salaries and buses {mcs_min_20260714}.

On Aug. 25, 2026, he said the district was 'having to cut 3.7 million dollars.' He urged caution on the cost of a new stadium scoreboard and said the public may face 'possibly having a referendum years from now.' {mcs_min_20260825}

On the same date he said that in 2025 the state allowed 'a half a billion dollars of tax-funded money to go to private and charter schools,' and he urged residents to talk to legislators about public schools {mcs_min_20260825}.
In 2022 he said he wanted the board to focus on 'finding ways to lift up those that may have unfortunately fallen through the cracks.' He also called for more career-oriented learning {ct_2022_qa}.
In July 2026 he praised the Grant Regional Career Center's programs and said the district should 'keep investing in that' {mcs_min_20260714}.
On Aug. 25, 2026, he said the stadium scoreboard replacement should cover the next 20 years without 'putting too much into it at a time when we're struggling.' {mcs_min_20260825}

on_incumbent: Is a current board member and the board's president {mcs_board}. In 2022 he said the board's relationships with teachers, administrators and superintendents gave it 'even more opportunity to put in opinions and help guide the direction of MCS.' {ct_2022_qa}
In August 2026 he thanked the transportation staff for the start of the school year {mcs_min_20260811}.
endorsements_finance: No endorsements or campaign finance reports were found.
gaps: No 2026 candidate website, questionnaire or forum appearance was found; his positions here come from board minutes and a 2022 questionnaire.

candidates.summary: Incumbent seeking another term in District 1, where voters choose three members {mcs_board}{ct_ballot_2026}.
background: Is a District I member of the Marion Community Schools board; the district lists him as joining in 2023 and does not list an occupation {mcs_board}. Board minutes refer to him as Dr. Richard Hart {mcs_min_20260714}.
path_to_ballot: BallotReady lists him as a District 1 candidate in 2018 and 2022 and shows his current term ending Dec. 31, 2026 {br_hart}.
Filed for reelection; The Indiana Citizen's copy of the state list gives May 29, 2026 as his filing date {incitizen_list}. The state lists him as Nonpartisan {in_list}.

items: On July 14, 2026, he called the decline in operating money 'troubling' and asked: 'Is there some way that we could put someone on the task of generating revenue from what we have?' He pointed to outside use of the Walton Center as an example {mcs_min_20260714}.

On Sept. 8, 2026, he objected to proposed revisions to the computer acceptable-use policy. He said the policy's wording could make board members who use personal computers for district business 'possibly criminally responsible' and encouraged the board 'to study it more before we bring it up for the next meeting.' {mcs_min_20260908}
On Aug. 11, 2026, he asked whether hiring a new insurance broker would end the district's other broker relationships {mcs_min_20260811}.
On Aug. 11, 2026, he made the motion, which passed unanimously, to approve the building-corporation lease amendments for facility improvements {mcs_min_20260811}.

on_incumbent: Is a current board member. The minutes this guide reviewed show him voting with the unanimous majority on the superintendent's contract extension and the 2026 facility financing {mcs_min_20260728}{mcs_min_20260811}.
endorsements_finance: No endorsements or campaign finance reports were found.
gaps: No candidate website, questionnaire, forum appearance or news profile was found for 2026. His 2022 Chronicle-Tribune questionnaire entry printed his name but no answers.
Occupation not confirmed. The district says he joined the board in 2023, while BallotReady lists him as a 2018 and 2022 candidate; whether he served before 2023 was not confirmed.
